hooks.text: A single teaspoon of a neutron star weighs one billion tons.
What happens when you crush an entire sun into a city?
A dead star only twelve miles wide actually weighs more than the Sun.

title: The Dead Star Heavier Than 900 Pyramids
description: One teaspoon of a neutron star weighs one billion tons, more than nine hundred Great Pyramids. Discover how these dense stars forged the world's gold.

beats.text: A single teaspoon of a neutron star weighs one billion tons.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a dense neutron star, NASA, 2020

beats.text: That is roughly nine hundred times the weight of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
beats.visual: aerial photograph of the Great Pyramid of Giza, 2015

beats.text: Neutron stars are the collapsed cores of supergiant stars that died in a supernova.
beats.visual: Hubble image of the Cassiopeia A supernova remnant, 2013

beats.text: In 1967, graduate student Jocelyn Bell Burnell detected a radio pulse so rhythmic she nicknamed it Little Green Men.
beats.visual: photograph of Jocelyn Bell Burnell with radio telescope equipment, 1967

beats.text: These remnants pack the mass of a sun into a city-sized sphere only 12 miles wide.
beats.visual: diagram comparing a neutron star size to Manhattan, NASA, 2018

beats.text: The star's gravity is so intense that the escape velocity exceeds half the speed of light.
beats.visual: artist's illustration of gravitational lensing around a neutron star, NASA, 2019

beats.text: In 2017, the LIGO observatory detected two of these giants colliding to forge the world's gold and platinum.
beats.visual: artist's illustration of two merging neutron stars, NSF, 2017

beats.text: These cosmic impacts created the heavy metals found in our jewelry today, but their origin remains unimaginably dense.
beats.visual: photograph of gold bullion bars and platinum nuggets, 2021

better_than_last: Corrected the loop by removing the dangling word 'when' and ensured every beat is supported by specific claims or prompt-provided facts.
